'''Ōi Shrine''' (大井神社) is a [[Shinto shrine]] with the name "Ōi" located in various places across Japan.

== Ōi Shrines List ==
* [[Ōi Shrine (Mito)]]（[[Ibaraki Prefecture|Ibaraki]] [[Mito, Ibaraki|Mito City]]） - A Shikinaisha (式内社) candidate shrine. The enshrined deity Kashima-no-Mikoto (建借馬命) had the former name Ōfu-no-Omi (意富臣), which later became "Ōi" through phonetic changes.
* [[Ōi Shrine (Kasama)]]（Ibaraki Prefecture [[Kasama, Ibaraki|Kasama City]]） - Shikinaisha candidate shrine.
* [[Oi Shrine]]（[[Shizuoka Prefecture|Shizuoka]] [[Shimada, Shizuoka|Shimada City]]） - Kokushi Genzaisha (国史見在社) and Beppyo Shrine (別表神社). Famous for the [[Shimada Obi Festival|Shimada no Obi Matsuri]]. There are several other shrines with the same name along the [[Ōi River (Shizuoka)|Ōi River]] basin.
* [[Ōi Shrine (Nagoya)]]（[[Aichi Prefecture|Aichi]] [[Nagoya|Nagoya City]]）
* [[Ōi Shrine (Aisai)]]（Aichi Prefecture [[:en:Aisai, Aichi|Aisai City]]）
* [[Oi Shrine]]（[[Gifu Prefecture|Gifu]] [[Kitagata, Gifu|Kitagata Town]] [[Motosu District, Gifu|Motosu District]]）
* [[Oi Shrine (Kyoto)]]（[[Kyoto Prefecture|Kyoto]] [[Kyoto|Kyoto City]] [[Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō Ward]]） - Shikinaisha candidate shrine. Named after the [[Ōigawa (Kyoto)|Ōi River (Kyoto)]].
* [[Ooi Shrine]]（Kyoto Prefecture [[Kameoka, Kyoto|Kameoka City]]） - Shikinaisha.
